decision: Use provenance-bound measured Qubes calibrations as the only resource inputs to fleet topology selection.

reviews.correctness: Prefer an end-to-end gate that applies each topology's measured RAM/vCPU/probe-latency profile before eligibility and ranking. This prevents synthetic planning values from winning after real calibration disagrees.
reviews.robustness_security: Fail closed on missing, duplicate, unexpected, or wrong-SHA calibration. Keep trust/co-residency constraints upstream of resource ranking and never let a cheaper topology bypass them.
reviews.latency_resources_regression: Reuse existing calibration reports and resource evaluator offline. This adds no qrexec round trips, workers, daemons, or production mutation paths; cost is linear in candidate workers/topologies.

alternatives.approach: Choose topology from static resource profiles, then inspect calibration manually
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Manual reconciliation can miss a probe-latency or RAM regression and allows stale planning assumptions to remain authoritative.

alternatives.approach: Run a second live Qubes benchmark solely for topology ranking
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Higher fidelity but adds VM/qrexec traffic, runtime variance, and operational complexity before the existing measured evidence has been consumed correctly.

alternatives.approach: Measured calibration -> calibrated topology -> existing resource-aware evaluator
alternatives.why: Strongest correctness/resource tradeoff with no production semantic change and deterministic QA.

qa: A RAM/CPU-ready topology with probeLatencyP95Ms above budget must be rejected.
A stable alternative within the same trust/correctness gates must win.
Missing, duplicate, unexpected, or wrong-SHA calibration must fail closed.
lessons: Collecting probe latency is insufficient unless the final topology authority consumes it.
Resource evidence must remain bound to the exact Git SHA and topology it calibrated.
Do not add live Qubes traffic when an offline deterministic gate can consume already-collected evidence.
